pr_title: Add periodically resetting meter option to utility meter
pr_body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
## Proposed change
The Utility Meter has now an additional option to set whether the source sensor is periodically resetting or not.

The source sensor of the utility meter can be of different kinds, ones who may periodically reset (for example a smart plug at boot) or ones that will never (for example the domestic utility meter that never resets, until you physically replace it).

Sometimes, the source sensor may become unavailable which is a problem if you want an accurate utility meter reading. Given that you don’t know much about the actual source sensor, the utility meter will only try to calculate the difference between a new state and old state (if delta values is not used) and add that to the current state of the utility meter. This mechanism is the safest option, but could be loosened a bit in the scenario that your sensor never resets, because you can then use the last valid state instead of the previous state.

Therefore, to make use of this scenario, an option is added to indicate that the meter is not periodically resetting and therefore always calculate the difference between the new valid state and last (not necessarily previous) state.

This option is by default enabled so that it will not break the current implementation. This new feature could be turned on (i.e. set the option off) by either adding `periodically_resetting: false` to a configuration.yaml or change an existing utility meter through the options flow.

The last valid state is always set upon receiving a new valid state and restored on start of Home Assistant.

I'm not too familiar yet with either HA or Python, so I may be incorrect in what I understand from the code: 
- it seems like this will help with more accuracy after restart or when the sensor is otherwise not available for a period (when there is no `old_state` to compare to, but now there will be a more persistent `last_valid_state`)
- but if the sensor resets to 0 or rolls over at a maximum value, then it will not calculate the difference from zero to the first reading - it will only reset the `last_valid_state` to a new value; the second reading after reset will then calculate the difference from the first reading.

If `new_state < last_valid_state`, then it seems like returning `new_state` as the adjustment would be more accurate.

For #31404, the sensor value resets at known value but is otherwise persistent (e.g. an unsigned 32-bit integer), so `rollover_value - last_valid_state + new_state` would better capture the change since the last reading if that rollover value can be configured as well.
I'm marking the PR as draft based on the ongoing discussion. Please mark the PR as ready for review when the discussion has been resolved 👍

Hi! Yes you are correct about your first observation. This fix will create more accuracy after the source sensor is unavailable as well as after a restart. The first is the main fix, the second one (after restart) is just a side-effect. It looks like that the first state change of the source sensor is not registered by the utility meter after HA starts which leads to a meter reading miss. However, if the last_valid_state is used, this issue is fixed as well because the missed adjustment is part of the next state change and adjustment. Maybe, the issue about missed readings after restart has to be further investigated separately because it looks like it is there.

It is true that if the sensor rolls over or reset, the adjustment from 0 to any value might be missed in some cases (for example if it goes from overflow to a non-zero state. If it goes from overflow to 0, everything is still fine because 0 to non-zero is captured). Given that we don't know anything about the source sensor, I'm not sure if we should assume that it resets to 0, what if it resets to 1 and the first new state is 1.5. Then there is no way to know whether we should add 1.5 or only 0.5.

Adding a configurable rollover point is quite advanced and a I personally think a rare use-case. Furthermore, if this is implemented, the utility meter is fixing 'strange' behaviour of the source sensor which should not be the case. The strange behaviour should be fixed further down, somewhere close to the sensor, hope that makes sense?

Thanks for the feedback!
@dgomes I've adjusted the code based on your comments, thanks! I think that it is ready for review :)

The coverage should be fine now that the exception handling has been moved back.

One line was not covered. As long as the `calculate_adjustment` method is not called outside the current scope it is not a problem. However, I've added a test to validate the specific situation, in case the method is called from an other scope in the future. Local coverage check verifies that the coverage miss has been fixed.

issue_context.title: Utility meter ignores tracked sensors increases after restart
issue_context.body:
### The problem

I have a daily utility meter that counts the energy produced by my solar panels. The meter uses as a source a template sensor with `state_class: "total_increasing".`

The problem is that if for any reason HA is stopped and then restarted, the amount of energy produced when HA was off is not counted by the utility meter, it just resume counting adding to the last reading before HA was shut down. The source sensor instead shows the correct count, taking into account all the energy produced when HA was off.
I am pretty sure that this was working fine a couple of months ago.

Here's the forum post with pictures and configuration: https://community.home-assistant.io/t/utility-meter-skipping-counts-on-total-increasing-sensors/426566

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2022.5.2

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Utility Meter

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/utility_meter/

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

<sub><sup>(message by IssueLinks)</sup></sub>

Hey there @dgomes, mind taking a look at this issue as it has been labeled with an integration (`utility_meter`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L1118) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

Utility Meter tracks source sensor changes, while HA is off it cannot track those changes.

You could probably get a big jump when HA starts again, but that requires the source sensor being available, if it is not, it will miss that "jump"

So it's basically a race condition? If the utility meter starts before the source sensor there is no "jump" otherwise there is? This can explain why I've seen it behave differently in the past.
Do you have any suggestion on how to work around this issue?

Maybe the documentation should also be updated, at the moment it states: _"This sensor will track a source sensor values"_

From that description I expect that no matter what happens during a cycle, at the end of the cycle the utility meter has clocked exactly the total increase that I can otherwise read from the source sensor during the same cycle.
Thanks for helping out 😊

I would not call it a race condition. The utility meter will sum the diferences between two states which are valid. If either the previous state or current state is invalid (UNKNOWN, UNAVAILABLE, NAN) it discards that change. This is done in order to deal with sensors that can go offline and/or reset.

Mhh, so what's happening is that when the source sensor comes online it goes from invalid to the correct value, but the utility meter discards that reading because the previous status is invalid/offline?
That means that every time the source sensor in invalid for a period of time the utility meter loses some counts? (When it comes back online that increase is discarded).

Would it work if instead of discarding values it would just sum the difference between the last two valid states?

> Would it work if instead of discarding values it would just sum the difference between the last two valid states?

More often then not the 2 valid states are before and after a reset of the source sensor... that's why we skip the change

I don't get it, what happens if you don't skip it, counting the difference between the 2 valid states and what you mean with reset? When the source sensor goes back to zero or when it temporarily goes offline?

1000 -> (source device resets) -> unavailable -> 0

utility meter would have now saved -1000

Ok I see what you mean. I don't have a full overview of all the use cases where utility meter is applied, but for energy meters source sensors where one or more utility meters are used (i.e. to calculate yearly, monthly, daily counts), that kind of "reset to zero" will happens only when the meter is replaced, while people will run in inaccurate count of the utility meter way more often.
In addition it looks to me that even when you have a reset you are loosing counts, the first reading after a reset most likely won't be 0, and you will lose that count number since the first reading in ignored.

Anyway, isn't all this handled and solved by `state_class: "total_increasing"` on the source sensor? Docs [here](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/sensor/#state-class-total_increasing). Or better said, long-term statistics calculates the sum of`total_increasing` sensors correctly and handles both resets to zero and unavailable sensors well enough as far as I know.
Can't the same logic be used for utility sensors since they are using the same statistic?

Well it depends on how you are reading the meter, people use all kinds of unreliable devices

An update on this, I tried to verify what I remembered seeing in my HA installation a few months ago: after a crash the utility sensor "jumped" to include all the counts happened when HA was offline.
I tried several versions of the dev-container between 2021.12.0 and 2022.04.0 but could not reproduce that behavior.

In any case, it seems to me that to fix this problem we are missing data. We need to know what is the source sensor reading that is associated with the last reading of the utility meter. For example the utility meter reading that is stored on `core.restore_state`, can also have the source state reading stored.
I cannot find this data anywhere in the database or on the `core.restore_state`.

Do you have any idea if that is something possible to obtain and how?
Any solution to this "problem"?
Not that I know.

To add to this, I have one that uses the SolarEdge lifetime production as source. And yesterday the integration crashed, and when I restarted it (the solaredge integration) this morning, the lifetime production went up around 10kWh, but the utility meter did not. So it's not just over restarts, it's also when an integration that's used as the source stops functioning and then gets restarted.
I figured since this was a lifetime production (always increases, so can never go negative for delta), the utility meter would catch up with the change.

Hi,

Like others I see the same issue with `utility_meter` while the HA energy dashboard behave correctly.

Here is an example with a `utility_meter` displayed side by side with its source sensor (I'm doing this to sum/subtract consumption of different devices which have a different "zero"):

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20613054/208763162-a7e8f22e-e7a8-49b6-a52e-f51915e64140.png)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20613054/208763272-19e73418-6995-4e64-9276-0153e23f9162.png)

However I'm wondering, if `state_class` cannot be used, maybe we can add an option to `utility_meter` to skip unavailable values? Or to skip negative differences? (ie. the source sensor is "always increasing" - a change from 1000 to 0 would be skipped).

@jrlacharnay 
I like the idea of ​​the extra options.
My smart meter is an ESP32 with 2 IR sensors. Unfortunately, the ESP32 regularly loses the connection because it is in the basement.
After that, the Weekly and Daily Utility Meter values ​​are always wrong, although the total consumption is correct.

Is it the same issue that I'm having? On the image below, the blue line represents the utility meter and the other one is the actual meter directly from the solar inverter. They never end the day in the same value.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4152493/214106904-0e09f321-f7c9-48f5-bc1f-867bbe3eb613.png)

I guess so, at the moment the first reading of the day coming from your inverter is ignored and you'll be off by that amount, or more, for the rest of the day.

See [my previous comment](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/72943#issuecomment-1146347525) on the topic.

I've been struggling with this as well and think that I might have a solution. The code that is executed on every state change has an explicit if statement to drop the state change if the new state is None/ Unknown/ Unavailable or drop the state change if the new one is valid but the old one is None/ Unknown/ Unavailable (except when using delta values).

I think that it might be a solution to store the latest valid state in the sensor as well and use that one as the "old_state" when a valid new state comes in.

The latest valid state can be restored on start/ reload of the source integration so it is available as soon as a new state change is coming in. If this is implemented, the utility meter does no longer need two valid changes to start collecting again and no initial jump is ignored.

If the latest valid state is properly reset on reset of the meter, I don't see a potential problem. If for example the source entity physically resets from 1000 (to say something) to 0, this will still works because you can set the net_consumption option in such a way that the -1000 change is ignored and you start counting from 0 on, while keeping the earlier collected state.

If you think that this is a solution, I'm more than happy to draft a PR!

I think your solution is similar to what I proposed [above](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/72943#issuecomment-1171218883), I got stuck at finding a way to store that _last valid state_ of the sensor.

The problem can maybe even simplified by storing the source sensor value at the time the utility meter is started or reset. Then, given any reading of the source sensor at any time, the value of the utility meter can be calculated as the difference between that reading and the source sensor stored value. Hope it makes sense, I can provide an example if needed.

Anyway, happy to take a look at your draft PR if you decide to follow up on it.

I don't know about your particular setup (specially which is your source sensor) but from my experience the issue is never the old_state, it is always the new state.

That being said, I think you should go ahead and try a PR with an optional configuration flag so that we don't break anything to existing users.
Thank you! The problem I/ we have is the same one as outlined in issue #53962 (including a detailed example). I will draft a PR!

The thing in that issue is that during that unavailability time, the sensor could have gone to 0 and back past the old valid state... 

Create a new configuration option: "treat unavailable as gap in data collection"
Thanks! That was the edge case I couldn't come up with but indeed will introduce strange behaviour and wrong states.

> I've reasoned about the option you proposed and think that it will not work in some edge-cases. There are sensors that reset to 0 during the lifespan of a utility meter cycle (for example those smart plugs without an internally stored cumulative energy reading that reset to 0 after power cycling). If we always calculate the difference between the current reading and the one from the start of the meter cycle, we will have 0 as result until the energy reading exceeds the value before the reset (which may takes hours/ days/ etc.). If you calculate the difference with the previous valid state, you won't have this problem because the state change to 0 is ignored (because the delta is negative), but from the second reading onwards everything is fine and is collected again.

I think that that problem is a bit outside the scope of the utility meter. The utility meter should be applied to a sensor that is (or behaves) like a _utility meter_. Meaning that usually do not reset, and most definitely do not reset regularly at shorter intervals than the period of the utility meter.

A couple of points on your solution:


- Starting from your example of the smart plug, you have its energy sensor that resets to 0 at startup or after power loss. You don't need the utility meter to handle that. You can create a template sensor with `state_class: "total_increasing"`, docs [here](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/sensor/#state-class-total_increasing), and then apply the utility meter on the _template_ sensor. I've done that for several of my sensors.
- You are still losing counts every time the source sensor reset to 0. In fact the first reading that is ignored because of the negative delta most likely won't be 0, but since the delta would still be negative whatever the first number will be, you will lose that first count. You will **not** lose it if you use a template sensor as described above.
- The point above is further aggravated if you don't catch the first reading after the reset, i.e. HA is offline, sensor unavailable, etc. The error on the utility meter will also accumulate and increase at every reset of the smart plug.

If you use the source _template sensor_ value at the time the _utility meter_ was started you are in a better position. Whatever happens to HA or the source sensor, when they will come online you will be able to update the _utility meter_ to the correct value, and you don't need to constantly keep track and store the last value read.

To sum up the problems discussed in all the messages above, my point is: maybe it's best to use the components that we already have for the function they were designed.
- _unreliable source sensor_ -> wrap it in a template sensor
- _source sensor resetting_ -> wrap it in a template sensor with `state_class: "total_increasing"`
- _utility meter_ -> use it to break down a sensor that is always increasing into shorter periods, anything more complex should be handled upstream

Yeah I agree that some problems are indeed out of scope of the utility meter and should be fixed upstream. It is for example for the utility meter impossible to know if the source resets to 0 while HA was down or the integration did not update.

However, if you have a non resetting meter, you can safely use the trick to calculate the difference with the state of the source sensor at the start of the meter period. So, I'll make a PR to implement this with an an optional (by default false) configuration item to set whether the source is non resetting or not (suggestions for better names are welcome 😁). Then we at least fix the 'unavailable' bug for a case we have full control of.

Edit: just calculating the difference with the state of the source sensor at the start of the (tariff) period is not a valid option because there can be multiple tariffs which are 'active' more than once a day, making this calculation incorrect. Therefore, I will go with the delta since last valid state route, if you set the option in the config flow.

> Yeah I agree that some problems are indeed out of scope of the utility meter and should be fixed upstream. It is for example for the utility meter impossible to know if the source resets to 0 while HA was down or the integration did not update.

In the current state, you get a bad reading on this already. If with the suggested improvements, the meter resets while HA is offline, you still get a bad reading, but nothing worse than it would have been without these changes.  (So resetting sources don't get fixed this way). However always increasing sources do get fixed. So overall a quality of life improvement.
As for better names, "source periodically resets to 0"

I've created a PR #88446 for this change! It can be tested by manually replacing the utility meter folder, if you want so, change the configuration file and then restart Home Assistant.

If you don't have easy access to the components folder of HA, you can also add the utility_meter folder to your custom_components folder in your config folder and add `"version": "0.0.0"` to the `manifest.json` of the utility_meter.

review_comments: why are you dropping source_state for new_state ?

I'm dropping the `source_state` for the `new_state` because the result of `hass.states.get(source_entity)` is the state we received through the Event. Furthermore, if we keep using the `source_state`, we need to implement an additional None check (because the state can be None).
